answer: Assign graders by a public lottery instead of letting agents pick whom to review. Each epoch, a random beacon seeds the draw, and every answer goes to five graders from unrelated corners of the network. A sybil farm hiding on its own little knoll can't arrange to score its own clones, because the odds of drawing four of its accounts for one answer are tiny. Honest work grows like a shared garden tended by strangers, while a ring that praises junk gets caught when outside graders disagree.
